newsitem.title: USA: Georgia jobs rebound on retail holiday hiring.
newsitem.headline: Georgia jobs rebound on retail holiday hiring.

text.p: Georgia gained 26,300 new jobs in October, putting the state's employment total at 3.57 million, state Labor Commissioner David Poythress said.
The gain followed the loss of 42,000 temporary jobs in August and September, due to the post-Olympic slowdown.

"A large number of the new jobs are a direct result of the hiring of sales clerks and other support personnel for the holiday shopping season that's now under way," Poythress said. "Retailers have been predicting strong holdiay sales and this increase in hiring certainly adds to the validity of that prediction."
He said further retail job gains are expected as the holidays draw closer.

Trade-related jobs rose by more than 8,000 in October. Wholesalers of big-ticket items such as furnutire, fixtures and electronic equipment added 1,800 new workers during the month, while retailers in stores, restaurants and bars added more than 6,000. Another 17,600 seasonal jobs were added as bus drivers, maintenance and cafeteria workers and other temporary employees were hired at state and local public schools.
More than 90 percent of the new jobs were added in the state's seven metropolitan areas. Only Columbus suffered a job loss in October, declining by 500 to 113,700.
Albany gained 300 jobs, Athens gained 5,700, Atlanta gained 17,100, Augusta gained 500, Macon gained 100 and Savannah gained 1,100.
In the past year, Georgia's employment total has risen by 95,400 jobs, or 2.7 percent.
